concepts.name: Number systems: why computers use binary
concepts.description: Why computers represent all data in binary (two-state switches, logic gates, registers); bits; the denary (base 10), binary (base 2) and hexadecimal (base 16) systems and place value. Conversions are in the next concepts.

concepts.name: Converting between binary and denary
concepts.description: Converting positive whole numbers between denary and binary in both directions, up to 16 bits, by place values and by repeated division by 2; writing 8-bit answers with leading zeros. Negative numbers and fractions are out.

concepts.name: Hexadecimal: conversions and uses
concepts.description: Converting positive whole numbers between hexadecimal and denary and between hexadecimal and binary (nibble groups); why hexadecimal is used (shorter, easier for humans to read than binary) and where: MAC addresses, colour codes, memory dumps, error codes, assembly code.

concepts.name: Octal (base 8)
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The octal number system: place values, converting between octal and denary and between octal and binary (groups of three bits), and comparing octal with hexadecimal.

concepts.name: Binary addition and overflow
concepts.description: Adding two positive 8-bit binary integers column by column with carries; recognising an overflow when the result needs more than 8 bits (greater than 255) and why overflow errors occur in a fixed-size register.

concepts.name: Binary subtraction
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Subtracting positive binary numbers column by column with borrowing, and checking the result by converting to denary. Two's complement subtraction is not required.

concepts.name: Logical binary shifts
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Logical left and right shifts (single and multiple places) on a positive 8-bit integer: bits lost at one end, zeros shifted in at the other, the effect (multiplying or dividing by a power of 2) and when a shift loses information.

concepts.name: Two's complement
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Representing positive and negative 8-bit integers in two's complement (range -128 to 127), converting between denary or binary and two's complement in both directions, and the meaning of the most significant bit.

concepts.name: Representing text: ASCII and Unicode
concepts.description: How text is stored as binary codes from a character set; ASCII (7-bit and extended 8-bit) and Unicode; why Unicode needs more bits per character and covers many more characters, languages and emojis; converting characters to codes using a given table.

concepts.name: Representing sound and images
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Sampling a sound wave: sample rate and sample resolution and their effect on accuracy and file size. Bitmap images as pixels: resolution and colour depth and their effect on quality and file size. File size calculations are in comp.data.file-size.

concepts.name: Units of data storage
concepts.description: Bit, nibble, byte and the larger units: kibibyte (KiB), mebibyte (MiB), gibibyte (GiB), tebibyte (TiB), pebibyte (PiB) and exbibyte (EiB) with 1024 between units (Cambridge), and the kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte and terabyte names used in the ZIMSEC syllabus; converting between units.

concepts.name: Calculating file sizes
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Calculating the file size of a bitmap image (resolution x colour depth) and of a sound file (sample rate x sample resolution x length), and giving the answer in the unit asked for using 1024.

concepts.name: Data compression: lossy and lossless
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Why files are compressed (less storage, less bandwidth, shorter transmission time); lossy compression (reducing resolution, colour depth, sample rate or resolution; permanent loss) and lossless compression, including run-length encoding (RLE); choosing a method for a given file.

concepts.name: Logic gates and their functions
concepts.description: The six gates NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR and XOR: their standard symbols (described in words), what each does, the truth table of each gate, and that NOT has one input while the others have two.

concepts.name: Truth tables for logic circuits and expressions
concepts.description: Completing a truth table with up to three inputs (A, B, C in binary order) for a logic circuit or a logic expression, using intermediate columns; checking a circuit's output for given inputs.

concepts.name: Designing logic circuits and writing logic expressions
concepts.description: Turning a problem statement, a logic expression or a truth table into a logic circuit (at most three inputs, one output, drawn as stated without simplification) and writing a logic expression from a problem statement, a circuit or a truth table; modelling control problems such as alarms and safety interlocks.

concepts.name: The central processing unit (CPU)
concepts.description: The role of the CPU in processing instructions and data; the microprocessor as an integrated circuit on one chip; the arithmetic logic unit, the control unit and main memory as processing devices. Register-level detail of the fetch-decode-execute cycle is in comp.hardware.fetch-execute.

concepts.name: Von Neumann architecture, the fetch-decode-execute cycle and CPU performance
concepts.description: Cambridge only. The Von Neumann CPU: ALU, CU, the registers PC, MAR, MDR, CIR and ACC, and the address, data and control buses; each step of the fetch-decode-execute cycle; how the number of cores, cache size and clock speed affect performance; what an instruction set is.

concepts.name: Embedded systems
concepts.description: Cambridge only. What an embedded system is (a microprocessor system with a dedicated function inside a larger device), its characteristics, examples (domestic appliances, cars, security and lighting systems, vending machines) and how it differs from a general-purpose computer.

concepts.name: Input devices
concepts.description: What an input device is and why it is needed; how common devices work and when to use them: keyboard, optical mouse, microphone, digital camera, barcode and QR code scanners, touch screens (resistive, capacitive, infra-red), 2D and 3D scanners; choosing a device for a scenario.

concepts.name: Output devices
concepts.description: What an output device is and why it is needed; how common devices work and when to use them: LCD and LED screens, DLP and LCD projectors, inkjet, laser and 3D printers, speakers and actuators; choosing a device for a scenario.

concepts.name: Sensors
concepts.description: Cambridge only. What a sensor is, the type of data each sensor captures (acoustic, accelerometer, flow, gas, humidity, infra-red, level, light, magnetic field, moisture, pH, pressure, proximity, temperature) and choosing the most suitable sensor for a context. Whole automated systems are in comp.emerging.automated-systems.

concepts.name: Primary storage (RAM and ROM) and virtual memory
concepts.description: Primary storage as memory directly accessed by the CPU; RAM (volatile, read-write) and ROM (non-volatile, read-only, holds the bootstrap) and why a computer needs both; virtual memory: pages moved between RAM and secondary storage when RAM is full (virtual memory is Cambridge only).

concepts.name: Secondary storage: magnetic, optical and solid-state
concepts.description: Why secondary storage is needed; how magnetic (hard disk: platters, tracks, sectors, electromagnets), optical (CD, DVD, Blu-ray: lasers, pits and lands) and solid-state (SSD, SD card, USB drive: NAND/NOR flash, control and floating gates) storage work; comparing them for capacity, speed, cost, durability and portability.

concepts.name: Ports, connections and the USB interface
concepts.description: Connecting peripherals to a computer through ports and cables (USB, HDMI, audio, Ethernet) and setting them up; the universal serial bus: how it transmits data (serial), and its benefits and drawbacks. Cambridge examines USB; ZIMSEC examines connecting hardware devices.

concepts.name: Data capture systems, POS terminals and ATMs
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. How hardware is combined in point-of-sale terminals, automated teller machines and data-capture systems (barcodes, OMR, OCR, MICR, magnetic stripe and chip cards, RFID), with their advantages and drawbacks in Zimbabwean shops, banks and schools.

concepts.name: Hardware and software maintenance and troubleshooting
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Common faults with software, keyboards, mice, hard drives and memory; diagnosing and fixing them; replacing faulty components safely; preventive maintenance; the parts of a PC and how it is assembled.

concepts.name: System software, application software and utilities
concepts.description: The difference between system software (operating systems, utilities, drivers, translators) and application software, with examples; common utility tools (anti-virus, disk defragmenter, disk clean-up, backup, compression, file managers) and what they do.

concepts.name: Off-the-shelf, customised and open-source software
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Types of application software by source: off-the-shelf (generic) packages, customised (bespoke) software and open-source software, with advantages and disadvantages of each; licences and freeware/shareware in outline.

concepts.name: Operating systems
concepts.description: The role and functions of an operating system: managing files, memory, peripherals and drivers, multitasking, interrupts, user accounts and security, providing an interface and a platform for applications; PC and mobile operating systems compared (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Firmware, the bootloader and interrupts
concepts.description: Cambridge only. How hardware, firmware (bootloader) and the operating system together run applications; what an interrupt is, how hardware and software interrupts are generated, how an interrupt service routine handles them and what happens as a result.

concepts.name: Programming languages, translators and IDEs
concepts.description: Cambridge only. High-level and low-level languages and their advantages and disadvantages; assembly language, mnemonics and assemblers; how a compiler and an interpreter translate code and report errors, and when each is used; the functions of an integrated development environment (editor, run-time environment, translator, error diagnostics, auto-completion, auto-correction, prettyprint).

concepts.name: Network types and topologies
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. What a computer network is and why networks are used; LAN, WAN, PAN and MAN; client-server and peer-to-peer networks; the star, ring, bus and mesh topologies with their advantages and disadvantages.

concepts.name: Transmission media
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Twisted pair, coaxial and fibre-optic cables and wireless media; comparing media on cost, bandwidth, noise immunity, distance, size and scalability; choosing a medium for a situation.

concepts.name: Mobile and wireless technologies
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Mobile phones, tablets, PDAs and satellite communication; wireless technologies (Wi-Fi, WiMAX, Bluetooth, infra-red, microwave and radio waves): range, speed and typical uses in communication.

concepts.name: Networking devices
concepts.description: The network interface card; hubs, switches, bridges, routers and modems and the job each does; how a router forwards data to its destination, can assign IP addresses and connects a local network to the internet; designing a simple network (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: MAC addresses and IP addresses
concepts.description: The MAC address (assigned at manufacture, manufacturer code and serial number, written in hexadecimal) and its purpose; the IP address (allocated by the network, static or dynamic); IPv4 and IPv6 compared.

concepts.name: Network protocols, TCP/IP and the OSI model
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. What a protocol is and why it is needed; the TCP/IP protocol suite and its layers; the seven layers of the OSI model in outline; common protocols (HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, POP3/IMAP) and what they do.

concepts.name: Internet service providers and internet services
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. What an internet service provider does (connection, email, hosting, domain names) and services such as email, e-commerce, e-learning and social media, with their benefits and risks.

concepts.name: Cloud storage and cloud services
concepts.description: What cloud computing and cloud storage are (remote physical servers accessed over the internet), examples of cloud services, and the advantages and disadvantages of storing data in the cloud compared with local storage.

concepts.name: Packets and packet switching
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Why data is broken into packets; the structure of a packet (header with destination address, packet number and originator's address; payload; trailer); packet switching: different routes chosen by routers, out-of-order arrival and reassembly.

concepts.name: Methods of data transmission
concepts.description: Serial and parallel transmission and simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex transmission modes; advantages and disadvantages of each and choosing the most suitable method for a scenario.

concepts.name: Error detection: parity, checksums, echo checks, check digits and ARQ
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Why errors occur in transmission (interference: data loss, gain or change); parity checks (odd, even, parity byte and parity block), checksums and echo checks; check digits for data entry (ISBN, bar codes); automatic repeat query with acknowledgements and timeouts.

concepts.name: Encryption
concepts.description: Why data is encrypted when transmitted; plaintext, ciphertext and keys; symmetric encryption (one shared key) and asymmetric encryption (public and private keys); digital signatures and certificates in outline (ZIMSEC system security).

concepts.name: The internet, the world wide web, URLs, HTTP(S), browsers and DNS
concepts.description: The internet as infrastructure and the world wide web as the pages on it; the parts of a URL; HTTP and HTTPS; what a web browser does (rendering HTML, bookmarks, history, tabs, cookies, navigation, address bar); how a page is located and displayed using DNS, IP addresses and the web server.

concepts.name: Cookies
concepts.description: What cookies are; session and persistent cookies; how they are used (saving personal details, tracking preferences, shopping baskets, login details) and the privacy issues they raise; managing cookies in a browser.

concepts.name: Digital currency and blockchain
concepts.description: Cambridge only. What a digital currency is (exists only electronically) and how it is used; blockchain in its basic form as a time-stamped digital ledger of records that cannot be altered, used to track transactions.

concepts.name: Malware
concepts.description: Viruses, worms, Trojan horses, spyware, adware and ransomware: how each works, what it aims to do, and its effects; anti-malware software (anti-virus and anti-spyware) as a defence.

concepts.name: Cyber attacks and computer crime
concepts.description: How brute-force attacks, data interception (sniffing), distributed denial of service, hacking, phishing, pharming, social engineering, spoofing and online fraud are carried out, what the attacker aims to achieve, and their effects on people and organisations.

concepts.name: Authentication and access control
concepts.description: Usernames and strong passwords, biometrics and two-step verification; access levels, user accounts and file permissions; privacy settings; choosing suitable controls for a scenario.

concepts.name: Firewalls, proxy servers, SSL and other protections
concepts.description: How firewalls and proxy servers protect a network; the secure socket layer (SSL) protocol and digital certificates; automatic software updates; checking URLs, spelling and tone of communications to spot attacks; matching each solution to the threats it counters.

concepts.name: Cyber-wellness and computer ethics (Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu)
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Responsible online behaviour: handling online content, online relationships, safe and unsafe websites, cyber-bullying; computer ethics and Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu values; the effects of unethical online activity on individuals and society.

concepts.name: Copyright, plagiarism and piracy
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Copyright and why it matters (Zimbabwe's Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act [Chapter 26:05] in outline; the syllabus resource list cites a Copyright Act, Chapter 26:1); plagiarism and software piracy, their consequences, and how anti-plagiarism software and licences help. Patents and other intellectual property rights for businesses are in comp.techno.laws-ipr.

concepts.name: Data privacy and data integrity
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Keeping personal data private (principles of data protection, consent, user accounts with access levels) and keeping data accurate and consistent (data integrity); threats to privacy and integrity. Validation and verification techniques are in comp.algorithms.validation-verification.

concepts.name: Backups and disaster recovery
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Backing up files (full and incremental backups, on-site, off-site and cloud), restoring data with recovery tools, and the contents of a disaster recovery plan.

concepts.name: Automated systems
concepts.description: Cambridge only. How sensors, a microprocessor and actuators work together in an automated system (read, compare with stored values, act, repeat), with scenarios from industry, transport, agriculture, weather, gaming, lighting and science, and the advantages and disadvantages of automation in a given scenario.

concepts.name: Robotics
concepts.description: What robotics is; the characteristics of a robot (mechanical structure, sensors, microprocessors, actuators, programmable); robots in industry, transport, agriculture, medicine, the home and entertainment, and the advantages and disadvantages of their use.

concepts.name: Artificial intelligence and expert systems
concepts.description: What artificial intelligence is; its characteristics (data and rules, reasoning, learning and adapting); expert systems (knowledge base, rule base, inference engine, interface) and machine learning; intelligent systems in use.

concepts.name: Computers in banking, education, social networks and research
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. How computer systems are used in banking (ATMs, EFT, internet and mobile banking, mobile money), education (e-learning, school administration systems), social networks and research and development, with benefits and drawbacks.

concepts.name: Computers in transport, health and environmental management
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Computer systems for transport management (ticketing, traffic control, tracking), health (patient records, monitoring, diagnosis support, health information systems) and environmental management (monitoring weather, pollution and resources).

concepts.name: Computers in manufacturing, mining and wildlife management
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Computer-aided design and manufacturing, process control in mining, and wildlife management (tracking collars, anti-poaching surveillance, park records), with benefits and drawbacks.

concepts.name: Computers in agriculture, ambient systems and GIS
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Computer use in agriculture (precision farming, irrigation control, livestock records, market information); ambient (smart) systems in homes and buildings; geographic information systems and their uses; designing models of such systems.

concepts.name: The systems development life cycle and fact-finding
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The stages of the systems development life cycle; problem identification and the preliminary investigation; fact-finding by questionnaire, interview, record inspection and observation, with advantages and disadvantages of each.

concepts.name: The feasibility study
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Technical, economic, legal, operational and social (and schedule) feasibility; carrying out a feasibility study and writing its conclusion.

concepts.name: Systems analysis: requirements, DFDs and activity diagrams
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Activities in the analysis stage: describing the current system, requirements, alternative solutions; drawing and interpreting data flow diagrams and activity diagrams (described in words or tables).

concepts.name: System design: input, output, interface, files and system flowcharts
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Designing input forms and output reports, user interfaces, files and database tables; system flowcharts; designing algorithms for the new system.

concepts.name: Documentation and user training
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. User documentation and technical documentation and their contents; why and how users are trained.

concepts.name: Implementation, evaluation and maintenance
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Changeover methods (direct, parallel, phased, pilot) with advantages and disadvantages; evaluating a new system against its objectives; corrective, adaptive and perfective maintenance.

concepts.name: Problem decomposition and the program development life cycle
concepts.description: The program development life cycle (analysis, design, coding, testing) and the tasks in each; systems made of sub-systems; abstraction and decomposition; inputs, processes, outputs and storage; structure diagrams; top-down and bottom-up design.

concepts.name: Algorithms and the sequence construct
concepts.description: What an algorithm is and why algorithms are used; the sequence construct; stating the purpose of a given algorithm and describing its processes; writing simple sequence algorithms in pseudocode.

concepts.name: Flowcharts
concepts.description: The standard flowchart symbols (terminator, process, input/output, decision, subroutine, flow line) described in words; drawing and interpreting flowcharts with sequence, selection and loops; converting between flowcharts and pseudocode.

concepts.name: Trace tables and dry runs
concepts.description: Dry-running an algorithm (pseudocode or flowchart) with given data and recording each change of the variables, outputs and user prompts in a trace table; using a trace to find the purpose of an algorithm or an error.

concepts.name: Totalling, counting, maximum, minimum and average
concepts.description: Standard methods: running totals, counting, finding the largest and smallest values and calculating an average, in loops over input values and arrays.

concepts.name: Linear search and bubble sort
concepts.description: The linear search (with a flag or early exit) and the bubble sort (passes, swaps, a flag to stop early): how they work, tracing them and writing them in pseudocode.

concepts.name: Validation and verification
concepts.description: Validation checks (range, length, type, presence, format, check digit) and why they are needed; verification checks (visual check, double entry) and their purpose; writing algorithms that validate or verify input.

concepts.name: Test data and test plans
concepts.description: Normal, abnormal, extreme and boundary test data and choosing values of each type; writing a test plan with expected results (ZIMSEC testing strategy).

concepts.name: Finding and correcting errors
concepts.description: Syntax, logic and run-time errors; identifying errors in a given algorithm or program and suggesting corrections; testing and debugging techniques and simple error handling.

concepts.name: Writing algorithms for scenarios
concepts.description: Writing and amending complete algorithms in pseudocode (or program code) for a described problem: planning the data structures, combining input with validation, loops, selection, arrays, totals and output; the Cambridge 15-mark scenario question and ZIMSEC project-style tasks.

concepts.name: Variables, constants, data types, input and output
concepts.description: Declaring and using variables and constants; the data types integer, real, char, string and Boolean (ZIMSEC: integer, character, string and Boolean); assignment; INPUT and OUTPUT; the structure of a simple program.

concepts.name: Operators and library routines
concepts.description: Arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /, ^, MOD, DIV), relational operators (=, <, <=, >, >=, <>) and logical operators (AND, OR, NOT); precedence and brackets; the library routines ROUND and RANDOM (Cambridge).

concepts.name: Selection: IF and CASE
concepts.description: IF statements with and without ELSE, nested IF statements and CASE statements with OTHERWISE, written in pseudocode; choosing between IF and CASE.

concepts.name: Iteration: FOR, WHILE and REPEAT loops
concepts.description: Count-controlled (FOR, with STEP), pre-condition (WHILE) and post-condition (REPEAT ... UNTIL) loops; choosing the right loop; nested loops (at most three levels).

concepts.name: String handling
concepts.description: Cambridge only. LENGTH, SUBSTRING, UCASE and LCASE; positions starting at 1 (or 0 in some languages); using string operations in loops (counting characters, extracting parts, checking formats).

concepts.name: Procedures, functions, parameters and scope
concepts.description: Defining and calling procedures and functions with or without parameters (up to three); RETURN values; local and global variables; why subroutines are used.

concepts.name: Writing maintainable programs
concepts.description: Meaningful identifiers for variables, constants, arrays, procedures and functions; comments; using subroutines and constants so that programs are easy to read, test and update; program structure.

concepts.name: One-dimensional arrays
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Declaring a 1D array with its bounds, reading and writing elements with a variable index, and processing an array with a loop (input, output, totals, search).

concepts.name: Two-dimensional arrays
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Declaring a 2D array, row and column indexes, and processing it with nested loops (filling, row and column totals, searching).

concepts.name: File handling
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Why programs store data in files; OPENFILE in READ or WRITE mode, READFILE, WRITEFILE and CLOSEFILE; reading and writing single items and lines of text.

concepts.name: Visual programming: interfaces, events and objects
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Designing user interfaces with menus and controls (forms, buttons, text boxes, labels, list boxes); event-driven programming; objects, properties and methods; classes, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism in outline (as in Visual Basic .NET or Python).

concepts.name: Database tables: fields, records, data types and primary keys
concepts.description: Defining a single-table database from given requirements: fields and records, suitable data types (text/alphanumeric, character, Boolean, integer, real, date/time), field sizes and formats, validation rules and input masks; choosing a suitable primary key.

concepts.name: Relational databases and entity-relationship diagrams
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Linking tables with primary and foreign keys; one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many relationships; entity-relationship diagrams with cardinality (described in words); database models compared; importing and exporting data.

concepts.name: Querying a table with SQL
concepts.description: Reading, completing and writing SQL to query a single table with SELECT, FROM, WHERE (with AND, OR), ORDER BY ASC/DESC, SUM and COUNT, and stating the output of a query on given data; designing and running queries in a database package (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Forms, reports and data manipulation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Creating datasheets, forms and reports; create, read (retrieve), update and delete (CRUD) operations; searching, sorting and filtering records.

concepts.name: Multi-table queries and connecting databases to programs
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Queries across related tables (joins, calculated fields, parameter queries, grouping) and connecting a database to a program so that it can read and update records.

concepts.name: Database security
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Protecting a database: user accounts and passwords, access rights and views, encryption, backups and audit of changes.

concepts.name: Web pages: elements, navigation and HTML
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The elements of a web page (headings, text, images, links, navigation bars, forms) and navigating a site; basic HTML tags and page structure; customising pages and using templates.

concepts.name: Content management systems, templates, plugins and graphics
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Building a website with a content management system (such as WordPress, Joomla or Drupal): templates, themes, plugins and extensions, web feeds and adverts; creating and optimising images, animations and video for the web.

concepts.name: Web security, testing and publishing
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Security measures in web development (HTTPS, strong admin passwords, updates, input checking, permissions), browser developer tools, testing and debugging a website (links, layout, forms, browsers and devices), and uploading and publishing a site.

concepts.name: Intellectual capital, business ethics and marketing
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Human, organisational and social capital; business ethics and Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu values; marketing and business strategies for ICT businesses, including e-commerce; the outline of an ICT business plan.

concepts.name: The technopreneurship ecosystem and innovation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Science parks, incubation centres, academic institutions and research and development centres and how they support technopreneurs; technology innovation and design thinking.

concepts.name: Laws, policies and intellectual property rights for technopreneurs
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Laws and policies that affect technology businesses (business registration, tax, consumer protection, cyber and data protection laws in outline); intellectual property rights: patents, copyright, trademarks and industrial designs, and how to protect an innovation.

concepts.name: Finance, funding and market research
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Sources of finance and funding for a technology start-up; conducting market research; choosing a business location.
